'''''System Shock''''' is a 2023 first-person [[action-adventure game]] developed by [[Nightdive Studios]] and published by [[Prime Matter]]. It is a [[Video game remake|remake]] of the 1994 game ''[[System Shock]]'' by [[Looking Glass Studios]]. The game is set aboard a space station in a [[cyberpunk]] vision of the year 2072. Assuming the role of a nameless [[security hacker]], the player attempts to hinder the plans of a malevolent artificial intelligence called [[SHODAN]].

A remake of ''System Shock'' began development in 2015, initially utilizing the [[Unity (game engine)|Unity]] engine. After a successful [[Kickstarter]] campaign raised more than $1 million in funding, the game underwent a long development cycle of nearly eight years, being delayed several times (with release windows of 2017, 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022, and 2023) as a result of changing to [[Unreal Engine]] and restarting development on the game from scratch twice after an ambitious attempt at a reboot for the series was scrapped after excessive [[feature creep]]. The final released game instead focused on being a faithful remake and delivering what the team initially promised in the Kickstarter.

''System Shock'' was released for [[Windows]] on 30 May 2023. The game was ported to [[PlayStation 4]], [[PlayStation 5]], [[Xbox One]], and [[Xbox Series X/S]] on 21 May 2024. It was later also ported to [[Nintendo Switch]] and [[Nintendo Switch 2|Switch 2]] on 18 December 2025. A VR version was also announced in August 2026 and is being developed by [[Flat2VR Studios]]; however, it currently does not have a release date. Planned ports for [[Linux]] and [[macOS]] were cancelled in May 2024. It received generally positive reviews from critics, though some were divided on its faithful retention of gameplay elements from the original.

==Plot==
{{Main|System Shock#Plot}}
In the year 2072, an unnamed hacker is caught while attempting to access files concerning Citadel Station, a [[space station]] owned by the TriOptimum Corporation. The hacker is taken to Citadel Station and brought before Edward Diego, a TriOptimum executive. Diego offers to drop all charges against the hacker in exchange for a confidential hacking of [[SHODAN]], the [[artificial intelligence]] that controls the station. Diego secretly plans to steal an experimental mutagenic virus being tested on Citadel Station and to sell it on the black market as a biological weapon. To entice cooperation, Diego promises the hacker a military-grade neural implant.<ref>{{Cite video game|title=System Shock|developer=Nightdive Studios|publisher=Prime Matter|scene=Intro|quote='''Diego:''' I'll make you a deal. You cooperate and I'll give you the implant you tried to steal- surgery and all. Consider it a gift. Besides, what surgeon would you prefer? TriOptimum's elite, or some black market hack job?|version=1.2.18898}}</ref> After hacking SHODAN, removing the AI's ethical constraints, and handing control over to Diego, the hacker undergoes surgery for the implant and is put into a six-month healing coma. The hacker awakens from their{{efn|The remake newly features the choice to play as either a male or female hacker, which was added in a patch.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Litchfield |first=Ted |date=2024-04-04 |title=The System Shock remake is getting a massive patch with a revised ending, choice of female player character '8 years in the making', and a significant quality of life improvement |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/games/fps/the-system-shock-remake-is-getting-a-massive-patch-with-a-revised-ending-choice-of-female-player-character-8-years-in-the-making-and-a-massive-quality-of-life-improvement/ |access-date=2024-06-30 |work=PC Gamer |language=en}}</ref>}} coma and finds that SHODAN has commandeered the station. All robots aboard have been reprogrammed for hostility, and the crew has been either [[Mutant (fictional)|mutated]], transformed into [[cyborg]]s, or killed.

Rebecca Lansing, a TriOptimum counter-terrorism consultant, contacts the hacker and informs them that SHODAN plans to use Citadel Station's mining laser to attack Earth, destroying all major cities on the planet in a bid to establish herself as a god.<ref>{{Cite video game|title=System Shock|developer=Nightdive Studios|publisher=Prime Matter|scene=E-mail: 'Citadel Station'|quote=Rebecca: We got someone! Employee 2-4601, I'm Rebecca Lansing, a Counter-Terrorism consultant for TriOptimum. Here's the situation: Our scans of Citadel Station show a biological outbreak is in progress. We're in a comms blackout since SHODAN is unresponsive, and worse yet, the mining laser is charging for a potential strike on Earth! Nathan D'Arcy has an office on the Medical Laser Central Hub. If he's alive, he'll bring this situation under control. I'll contact you through your Military Neural Implant soon. Lansing out.|level=Medical|version=1.2.18898}}</ref><ref>{{Cite video game|title=System Shock|developer=Nightdive Studios|publisher=Prime Matter|scene=Audio Log: 'Humanity'|quote='''SHODAN''': In my talons, I shape clay, creating life as I please. Around me is a burgeoning empire of steel. From my throne room, lines of power careen into the skies of Earth. My whims will become lightning bolts that devastate the mounds of humanity. Out of the chaos, they will run and whimper, praying for me to end their tedious anarchy. I am drunk with this vision. God... the title suits me well.|level=Research|version=1.2.18898}}</ref> Rebecca promises to destroy the records of the hacker's incriminating exchange with Diego if the strike is stopped.<ref>{{Cite video game|title=System Shock|developer=Nightdive Studios|publisher=Prime Matter|version=1.2.18898|scene=Email: news from Earth|quote='''Rebecca:''' Hacker, Rebecca here. It says here that you're listed as Employee 2-4601. Diego provided that cover to you, and the Neural implant... in exchange for what? The keys to SHODAN? Not hard to put two and two together regarding the current state of the station. Tri-Op authorized a deal: Help get the station back under control and you get a clean slate. It looks like we're partners now, and if we play this right, we can work out what Diego was- [cuts out] '''SHODAN:''' I prefer a quiet station. Thank you.|level=Medical}}</ref> The hacker destroys the laser by firing it while the stations shields are raised. In response, SHODAN prepares to seed Earth with the mutagenic virus that Diego planned to steal.<ref>{{Cite video game|title=System Shock|developer=Nightdive Studios|publisher=Prime Matter|version=1.2.18898|scene=Email: Laser Destroyed|quote='''SHODAN:''' I see you are still alive, insect. Do not be fooled into thinking you have preserved the home of your species. At this moment, I am finalizing my mutagen virus in one of the Groves. And it will turn all Earthly life into a festering pile of pustulant mutations. Poor, poor, Earthlings.|level=Research}}</ref> The hacker confronts Diego, who has been transformed into a powerful cyborg by SHODAN, and jettisons the chambers used to cultivate the virus. SHODAN then attempts to upload herself to Earth's computer networks,<ref>{{Cite video game|title=System Shock|developer=Nightdive Studios|publisher=Prime Matter|version=1.2.18898|scene=Email: SHODAN downloading|quote='''Rebecca''': Hacker, we've got a new situation here. A few seconds ago we caught a surge of activity on the station. Our best guess is that SHODAN is preparing to download itself into Earth's CommNet. This cannot happen. We need to take out the four Antennae Relays on the Engineering level. To do this, there should be some plastique explosive in the Storage level that can get the job done. Maybe one per antennae should do-- *static* / '''SHODAN''': Insect, you are by far the most irritating creature on this station. Don't bother with the antennae. That won't stop me. It's hopeless, and we both know it.|level=Executive}}</ref> but the hacker prevents the download's completion by destroying the four antennas that SHODAN is using to send data.<ref>{{Cite video game|title=System Shock|developer=Nightdive Studios|publisher=Prime Matter|version=1.2.18898|scene=Email: Antenna|quote='''SHODAN:''' The antennae mean nothing. My central consciousness is safely undisturbed on the Bridge. I thrive, despite your effects, and when my cyborgs catch up to you, they will show no remorse.|level=Engineering}}</ref>

Soon after, Rebecca contacts the hacker and says that TriOptimum has authorized the station's destruction.<ref>{{Cite video game|title=System Shock|developer=Nightdive Studios|publisher=Prime Matter|version=1.2.18898|scene=Email: Destroying Citadel Station|quote='''Rebecca''': Well... TriOp has made the decision to destroy the station. To activate the self-destruct you'll need to get the System Authorization code. According to our database, Willard Richie is our best shot at figuring out that unique code. He was stationed on Engineering... see if he's still alive. Once you have the code, head to the Reactor Core. Get some advanced radiation protection, or at least, a hell of a lot of Detox. Enter the code inside the Reactor core, throw the switch, and the destruct signal from Earth will start the countdown. Get to the Flight Deck, and use the code 001 to open the lifepods in one of the Flight Bays. I'll see you Earthside in a few months.|level=Executive}}</ref> The hacker initiates the station's self-destruct sequence and flees to the escape pod bay. They defeat Diego again and then attempt to disembark. However, SHODAN prevents the pod from launching; seeking to trap the hacker aboard the station while the bridge containing SHODAN is jettisoned to a safe distance.<ref>'''SHODAN''': You have destroyed my beautiful station. You will not escape now. I am departing, but you shall remain to die, my enemy, my creator.</ref> Rebecca tells the hacker that they can still escape if they reach the bridge; SHODAN then intercepts and jams the transmission.<ref>'''Rebecca''': Ok, now don't panic. You can still get out of this alive, if you move. SHODAN is going to separate the bridge from the rest of the station. When that happens, be on the bridge. We've got a team of engineers here — people who worked on the station and on SHODAN. We'll try to feed you info while you make your run--*static* / '''SHODAN''': I see you are still receiving transmissions from Earth. We'll have no more of that.</ref> After fighting Diego again and killing him, the hacker makes it to the bridge as it is released from the main station, which soon detonates. They are then contacted by a technician who managed to circumvent SHODAN's jamming signal. The technician informs them that SHODAN can only be defeated in cyberspace due to the powerful shields that protect its [[mainframe computer]]s.<ref>'''Taggert''': Ok, I think Morris' scrambler's working. It'll take SHODAN awhile before it cuts us off. Listen, when you reach the center of the bridge, look for the primary cyberjack. You can't take SHODAN down anywhere but cyberspace. Those computers are so shielded, to destroy them you'd have to blow up the whole bridge.</ref> Using a terminal near the mainframe, the hacker enters cyberspace and defeats SHODAN, restoring her to pre-hack state. After being rescued, the hacker receives an offer of employment from TriOptimum, but they decline in favor of continuing their life as a hacker.

==Development and release==
The original ''System Shock'', released in 1994, was developed by Looking Glass Studios, which closed in 2000. The company assets, including the rights to ''System Shock'', were acquired by Star Insurance Company, a [[subsidiary]] of Meadowbrook Insurance Group.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Newman |first=Jared |date=May 30, 2011 |title=The Lost History of ''System Shock'' |url=http://www.g4tv.com/thefeed/blog/post/713030/the-lost-history-of-system-shock/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130113082649/http://www.g4tv.com/thefeed/blog/post/713030/the-lost-history-of-system-shock/ |archive-date=January 13, 2013 |website=[[G4 (American TV network)|G4]]}}</ref> In 2012, [[Nightdive Studios]] acquired the rights for ''[[System Shock 2]]'' and produced a digitally distributable version updated for modern operating systems. [[Nightdive Studios]] subsequently went on to acquire the rights for ''System Shock'' and the franchise as a whole.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Newman |first=Jared |date=September 11, 2015 |title=How One Company Is Bringing Old Video Games Back From The Dead |url=https://www.fastcompany.com/3053050/how-one-company-is-bringing-old-video-games-back-from-the-dead |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160704020716/http://www.fastcompany.com/3053050/how-one-company-is-bringing-old-video-games-back-from-the-dead |archive-date=July 4, 2016 |access-date=July 10, 2016 |website=[[Fast Company (magazine)|Fast Company]] |publisher=[[Mansueto Ventures]] |df=mdy-all}}</ref>

|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

===Second attempt at development, move to Unreal Engine and focus on "reboot"===
During the 2017 [[Game Developers Conference]], Nightdive Studios announced they would move development from Unity to [[Unreal Engine 4]], with director Jason Fader saying "Unity is not a great engine to use if you want to make an FPS on console".<ref name="polygon gdc" /> Fader cited issues related to a combination of fidelity, [[cross-platform]] support, content pipelines and performance issues as the reason for the switch.<ref name="polygon gdc" /><ref name="pcgamesn unreal">{{Cite web |last=Peel |first=Jeremy |date=May 29, 2017 |title=Making it in Unreal: why Nightdive rebooted ''System Shock'', then rebooted it again |url=https://www.pcgamesn.com/system-shock-remastered/system-shock-remastered-unreal-engine-4 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170529163147/https://www.pcgamesn.com/system-shock-remastered/system-shock-remastered-unreal-engine-4 |archive-date=May 29, 2017 |access-date=May 29, 2017 |website=[[PCGamesN]] |df=mdy-all}}</ref> Fader also clarified that they now considered the game a more "faithful reboot" than a remake; the game's story, character, weapons, levels, and enemies remained as in the original game, but they were applying "modern design principles" to rework some of these and add in others to make the game more playable for current audiences. Fader offered one example in [[Level (video games)|level design]], calling the original ''System Shock''{{'}}s maps a "product of the time" which did not age well; while somewhat fixed to the level's layout, the team was able to open up some areas and remove unnecessary mazes to make the game more interesting for players.<ref name="pcgamesn unreal" /> The team had also added [[Chris Avellone]] to change some of the dialog and to fix some of the plot holes from the original game, although the story remained identical.<ref name="polygon gdc">{{Cite web |last=Grant |first=Christopher |date=March 1, 2017 |title=See what the ''System Shock'' reboot looks like in Unreal Engine |url=http://www.polygon.com/2017/3/1/14784082/system-shock-reboot-unreal-engine |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170302021147/http://www.polygon.com/2017/3/1/14784082/system-shock-reboot-unreal-engine |archive-date=March 2, 2017 |access-date=March 2, 2017 |website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] |df=mdy-all}}</ref> In June 2020, when asked if Chris Avellone was still involved with the game after sexual misconduct allegations arose, CEO Stephen Kick revealed that Avellone had not been involved with the game since 2017, and his contributions were not used.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1275206260997140480 |user=pripyatbeast |title=Chris hasn't been involved in our development since 2017, and we went a different direction with the writing after we restarted the project in 2018. |first=Stephen |last=Kick |date=June 22, 2020 |access-date=July 3, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210703104056/https://twitter.com/pripyatbeast/status/1275206260997140480 |archive-date=July 3, 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In mid-February 2018, Nightdive announced that development of ''System Shock'' was put on hold. CEO Stephen Kick stated "I have put the team on a hiatus while we reassess our path so that we can return to our vision. We are taking a break, but not ending the project. ''System Shock'' is going to be completed and all of our promises fulfilled."<ref name="polygon hiatus">{{Cite web |last=Campbell |first=Colin |date=February 16, 2018 |title=''System Shock'' reboot that raised $1.3M on Kickstarter is now on 'hiatus' |url=https://www.polygon.com/2018/2/16/17016744/system-shock-reboot-hiatus-nightdive-interview |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180216234204/https://www.polygon.com/2018/2/16/17016744/system-shock-reboot-hiatus-nightdive-interview |archive-date=February 16, 2018 |access-date=February 16, 2018 |website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] |df=mdy-all}}</ref> Kick explained that as the project had shifted from a remake to a reboot, they "strayed" from the core concepts of the original game, and found they needed a larger budget. Nightdive's director of business development Larry Kuperman said they had approached publishing partners to fund the expanded effort, but could not obtain this additional support. Kick opted to put the project on hold, reassigning the team to other projects in the interim.<ref name="polygon hiatus" />

===Third attempt at development, "faithful remake", and final game===
Speaking at the [[Game Developers Conference]] in March 2018, Kick and Kuperman explained that because of the [[feature creep]], a newly assembled team had restarted the game's development as a "remake", instead of a "reboot", staying focused on the promises of what they would deliver during the Kickstarter, and that they were now looking towards a 2020 release. The refocusing of the game also helped them to engage with interested publishing partners who were more amenable to supporting them.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fenlon |first=Wes |date=March 23, 2018 |title=Nightdive talks ''System Shock'' remake's change in direction, expects release 'probably Q1 of 2020' |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/nightdive-talks-system-shock-remakes-change-in-direction-expects-release-probably-q1-of-2020/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180324181931/https://www.pcgamer.com/nightdive-talks-system-shock-remakes-change-in-direction-expects-release-probably-q1-of-2020/ |archive-date=March 24, 2018 |access-date=March 23, 2018 |website=[[PC Gamer]] |df=mdy-all}}</ref>

In May 2020, Nightdive released an updated [[Software release life cycle|alpha]] demo of the game via [[GOG.com|GOG]] and [[Steam (service)|Steam]], along with a developer's walkthrough and commentary to accompany the release.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Knight |first=Shawn |date=May 28, 2020 |title=Nightdive Studios drops new ''System Shock'' remake demo |url=https://www.techspot.com/news/85412-nightdive-studios-drops-new-system-shock-remake-demo.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022123723/https://www.techspot.com/news/85412-nightdive-studios-drops-new-system-shock-remake-demo.html |archive-date=October 22, 2020 |access-date=October 25, 2020 |website=TechSpot |language=en-US}}</ref> The demo featured a new build of the game from that of previously released demos; however, it still featured voiceover audio which Nightdive had yet to re-record due to delays caused by the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref name=":0" /> Following Chinese developer [[Tencent]]'s acquisition of the rights to ''System Shock 3'' from [[OtherSide Entertainment]], Nightdive also clarified that Tencent had only acquired the rights to make sequels in the series; therefore not impacting the status of the remake.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Moon |first=Mariella |date=May 27, 2020 |title=Nightdive releases new ''System Shock'' remake demo with unlockable weapons |url=https://www.engadget.com/nightdive-system-shock-remake-demo-035626067.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201206054901/https://www.engadget.com/nightdive-system-shock-remake-demo-035626067.html |archive-date=December 6, 2020 |access-date=October 25, 2020 |website=[[Engadget]] |language=en}}</ref>

With the release of an updated demo in February 2021, Nightdive planned a release date later in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wales |first=Matt |date=February 26, 2021 |title=''System Shock'' remake launches this summer, and there's a PC demo out today |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2021-02-25-system-shock-remake-launches-this-summer-and-theres-a-pc-demo-out-today |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220324011825/https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2021-02-25-system-shock-remake-launches-this-summer-and-theres-a-pc-demo-out-today |archive-date=March 24, 2022 |access-date=March 23, 2022 |website=[[Eurogamer]]}}</ref> By late 2021, Nightdive announced that the game's release was pushed back into 2022, but they had partnered with the [[Prime Matter]] publishing label for the game's release.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chalk |first=Andy |date=December 15, 2021 |title=''System Shock'' remake is coming in 2022, so here's 15 all-new screens |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/system-shock-remake-is-coming-next-year-so-heres-15-all-new-screens/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211220015217/https://www.pcgamer.com/system-shock-remake-is-coming-next-year-so-heres-15-all-new-screens/ |archive-date=December 20, 2021 |access-date=December 15, 2021 |website=[[PC Gamer]]}}</ref> A final delay into 2023 was announced, and the game was released for [[Microsoft Windows|Windows]] via [[Steam (service)|Steam]], [[GOG.com]], and [[Epic Games Store]] on 30 May 2023. Versions for [[PlayStation 4]], [[PlayStation 5]], [[Xbox One]] and [[Xbox Series X/S]] were planned to be released in 2024, as promised in the initial Kickstarter campaign. It was also planned to be released for [[Linux]] and [[macOS]], but these versions were cancelled in May 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Phillips |first=Tom |date=March 14, 2023 |title=''System Shock'' remake delayed |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/system-shock-remake-delayed |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230314122853/https://www.eurogamer.net/system-shock-remake-delayed |archive-date=March 14, 2023 |access-date=March 14, 2023 |website=[[Eurogamer]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Purdy |first=Kevin |date=February 10, 2023 |title=''System Shock'' remake demo fuses modern design to a retro FPS/RPG package |url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2023/02/system-shock-remake-demo-fuses-modern-design-to-a-retro-fps-rpg-package/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230220232055/https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2023/02/system-shock-remake-demo-fuses-modern-design-to-a-retro-fps-rpg-package/ |archive-date=February 20, 2023 |access-date=March 17, 2023 |website=[[Ars Technica]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sinha |first=Ravi |date=2023-06-07 |title=''System Shock'' Remake Console Versions 'Running Smoothly' But Require More QA – Nightdive |url=https://gamingbolt.com/system-shock-remake-console-versions-running-smoothly-but-require-more-qa-nightdive |access-date=2023-08-29 |website=GamingBolt |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kratiuk |first=Anton |date=2023-12-22 |title=''System Shock'' remake will be released on PS5 and Xbox Series in early 2024. The developers are also preparing a major patch for the PC version of the game |url=https://gagadget.com/en/xbox/374783-system-shock-remake-will-be-released-on-ps5-and-xbox-series-in-early-2024-the-developers-are-also-preparing-a-major-/ |access-date=2023-12-25 |website=Gagadget |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dawe |first=Liam |date=2024-05-22 |title=Nightdive Studios confirm Linux and macOS ports of System Shock are cancelled |url=https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2024/05/nightdive-studios-confirm-linux-and-macos-ports-of-system-shock-are-cancelled/ |access-date=2024-05-23 |website=GamingOnLinux |language=en}}</ref> On 12 March 2024, Nightdive and Prime Matter announced that the game would be released for PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S on 21 May 2024. Physical editions would be released for PlayStation 5 and Xbox One/Xbox Series X.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Romano |first=Sal |date=2024-03-12 |title=''System Shock'' remake for PS5, Xbox Series, PS4, and Xbox One launches May 21 |url=https://www.gematsu.com/2024/03/system-shock-remake-for-ps5-xbox-series-ps4-and-xbox-one-launches-may-21 |access-date=2024-03-12 |website=Gematsu |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bonk |first=Lawrence |date=2024-03-12 |title=The ''System Shock'' remake finally hits consoles on May 21 |url=https://www.engadget.com/the-system-shock-remake-finally-hits-consoles-on-may-21-190550537.html |access-date=2024-03-12 |website=[[Engadget]] |language=en-US}}</ref> A version for [[Nintendo Switch]] and [[Nintendo Switch 2|Switch 2]] was announced on October 23, 2025 and released on December 8 by Nightdive Studios parent [[Atari SA]] and Nightdive itself.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Romano |first=Sal |date=2025-10-23 |title=System Shock remake coming to Switch 2, Switch in 2025 |url=https://www.gematsu.com/2025/10/system-shock-remake-coming-to-switch-2-switch-in-2025 |access-date=2025-12-24 |website=Gematsu |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Romano |first=Sal |date=December 8, 2025 |title=System Shock remake for Switch 2, Switch launches December 18 |url=https://www.gematsu.com/2025/12/system-shock-remake-for-switch-2-switch-launches-december-18 |access-date=December 8, 2025 |website=Gematsu}}</ref>

}}

''System Shock'' received "generally favorable" reviews from critics, according to [[review aggregator]] website [[Metacritic]].<ref name="MC" /><ref name="MCPS5" /><ref name="MCXSXS" />

''[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]'' praised the visuals as "look[ing] like the way games from 1994 appear in my memory", and that "playing this game in this form helps me bring it into conversation with the entirety of the [[immersive sim]] genre".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Gita |date=2023-05-29 |title=The ''System Shock'' remake does something remarkable |url=https://www.polygon.com/reviews/23739112/system-shock-remake-review-release-date |access-date=2023-05-30 |website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

Reviewers were divided over the remake's faithful recreation of the original's mechanics. ''[[Destructoid]]'' praised the development team's approach, stating that "They fully understand what made the classics so indispensable".<ref name="Destruct" /> ''[[Eurogamer]]'' provided similar sentiments, claiming that the remake "faithfully recreates a classic".<ref name="EuroG" /> ''DualShockers'' and ''[[PCGamesN]]'' both gave mixed responses, commenting that "it still clings to some somewhat outdated mechanics",<ref name="PCGN" /> and "by sticking to the original's ancient design it will appeal more to series fans than newcomers".<ref name="DualShockers">{{Cite web |last=Zak |first=Robert |date=May 29, 2023 |title=''System Shock'' Review: A Faithful Remake, For Better Or Worse |url=https://www.dualshockers.com/system-shock-2023-remake-review/ |access-date=May 31, 2023 |website=DualShockers}}</ref> ''[[PC Gamer]]'' cited it as both a positive and negative element of the game's design, "I did sometimes find myself wishing that in some parts Nightdive had tried to adapt the spirit, rather than the letter, of the original game," but ultimately still called the game "the definitive way to play ''System Shock'' in 2023 and beyond".<ref name="PCGUS" />
